item.text:
The HVAC demand flexibility measures are **upgrades 24–28**. They differ in whether they reduce HVAC use **during peak hours** or precondition the home **before peak hours**, and in the temperature offset and duration. [ResStock release list](https://resstock.nlr.gov/datasets)

| Upgrade | Measure ID | Strategy | Thermostat adjustment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **24** | `dr_001` | On-peak load shedding, 2°F | Lower heating / raise cooling setpoint by **2°F during the peak window**; no preconditioning |
| **25** | `dr_002` | 4-hour pre-peak load shifting, 2°F | Raise heating / lower cooling setpoint by **2°F for 4 hours before the peak** |
| **26** | `dr_003` | On-peak load shedding, 4°F | Lower heating / raise cooling setpoint by **4°F during the peak window**; no preconditioning |
| **27** | `dr_004` | 4-hour pre-peak load shifting, 4°F | Raise heating / lower cooling setpoint by **4°F for 4 hours before the peak** |
| **28** | `dr_005` | 1-hour pre-peak load shifting, 2°F | Raise heating / lower cooling setpoint by **2°F for 1 hour before the peak** |

The final measure documentation specifies **4-hour on-peak shedding windows** for 24 and 26. For the shifting measures, the thermostat returns to its normal schedule during the peak; stored heat or cooling helps reduce peak demand. The final scenarios do **not combine preconditioning with an on-peak setback**. [HVAC Load Flexibility documentation, Table 8](https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy26osti/93846.pdf#page=33)

Thus, **24 versus 26** tests a stronger shedding offset; **25 versus 27** tests a stronger preconditioning offset; and **25 versus 28** tests longer preconditioning. Shedding permits cooler winter or warmer summer conditions during the event, while shifting moves conditioning earlier.

For analysis, these measures are dispatched nearly every day to expose technical potential. Use selected event-day profiles rather than treating their annual savings as a typical demand-response program’s savings. [Release README](https://oedi-data-lake.s3.amazonaws.com/nrel-pds-building-stock/end-use-load-profiles-for-us-building-stock/2025/resstock_amy2018_release_1/README_resstock_20251.pdf)
